content.text:
Content-Type parameters with quoted values now parse per RFC 9110, and the new and existing tests pass.

The parser in `lib/content-type.js` no longer splits on `;` with a regex. It scans the parameter list left to right:

- **Quoted values:** a `;` inside quotes stays part of the value, and parsing resumes correctly after the closing quote.
- **Inner text:** nothing inside a quoted value is treated as a separate parameter, so `title="lang=en; charset=latin1"` gives only `title`.
- **Escapes:** `\"` and other backslash escapes inside quoted values are unescaped.
- **Existing behaviour kept:** token values are read as before, and an unterminated quote still yields `invalid quoted string` and parsing continues at the next `;`.

I added three tests to `test/content-type.test.js`, covering both examples from the report and escaped quotes. I ran that file together with `test/content-parser.test.js` (57 tests, all pass), and eslint is clean on the changed files.

I did not run the full test suite.
